punchline: A district manager's eight-page telex became Intel's Operation Crush, and by the end of 1980 Motorola had lost.
thirty_sec: In late 1979 Intel's 8086 chip was losing to Motorola. District sales manager Don Buckout sent an eight-page telex, it reached Andy Grove, and the company set one objective and a target of 2,000 design wins. Crush teams went out to field offices in January 1980, and by the end of the year Intel had beaten Motorola. The cheaper 8088 later powered the first IBM PC.
